threads_text: OpenAI dropped its planned cut to ChatGPT Pro 200 and doubled the Work and Codex limits on Pro 100 and Pro 500 instead, at the same prices. Plus users get nothing new. Would you pay $100 a month for ChatGPT?
caption:
OpenAI canceled a planned usage cut for ChatGPT Pro 200 after users pushed back.
Pro 100 and Pro 500 now get twice their old Work and Codex allowance, at the same price.
Plus stays exactly where it was.

Is a Pro plan worth it for you?

site_article.headline: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro usage limits and cancels a planned Pro 200 cut
site_article.dek: Pro 100 and Pro 500 subscribers get twice their previous Work and Codex allowance at the same prices, while the Plus plan stays unchanged.
site_article.summary: On October 29, 2026, OpenAI reversed a planned reduction to the usage allowance on its ChatGPT Pro 200 plan and doubled the Work and Codex allowances on Pro 100 and Pro 500. Prices did not change, and the $20 Plus plan was left as it was.
site_article.seo_title: ChatGPT Pro limits doubled, Pro 200 cut canceled
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI doubled Work and Codex allowances on ChatGPT Pro 100 and Pro 500, canceled a planned Pro 200 cut and left Plus unchanged.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes, OpenAI raised ChatGPT Pro limits on October 29, 2026: Pro 100 and Pro 500 get twice their previous Work and Codex allowance, and Pro 200 subscribers on the lower allowance were moved up to the higher one. Plus usage did not change.
site_article.hero_alt: ChatGPT open on a computer screen.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI doubled the Work and Codex usage allowances on its ChatGPT Pro 100 and Pro 500 plans on October 29, 2026, and called off a planned reduction for the Pro 200 plan, according to The Decoder and Kingy AI. The Decoder reports that the reversal followed pushback from users.

The Pro 200 change had been announced in September. Kingy AI, citing earlier reporting, says the plan would have moved the Pro 200 allowance from a level historically described as 20 times Plus down to 10 times Plus. CellCog dates that announcement to September 29, the day OpenAI launched the Pro 500 tier and reopened Pro 200 with a lower allowance. Eligible existing customers had been protected from the cut through October 29.

Under the new terms, Pro 100 and Pro 500 subscribers receive twice their previous Work and Codex allowance. Pro 200 subscribers who were on the lower allowance have been raised to match the higher one, and those already on the higher allowance keep it. Business Premium is also named in the change, although CellCog notes that OpenAI's pages give no per seat figure for it.

Prices did not change. Plus remains $20 a month, and the three Pro tiers cost $100, $200 and $500 a month, according to Kingy AI and CellCog. Existing subscribers receive the higher allowance automatically, without waiting for a renewal, and new subscriptions include it from the start.

Several things stay the same. The Plus plan's usage is unchanged, and CellCog reports that weekly GPT-6 Pro message limits in chat on Pro 100 and Pro 500 are not affected, nor is Ultrafast access, which remains limited to Pro 500. The Decoder adds that expanded limits for OpenAI's Dots agents stay in place for now, with Dot usage tracked separately.

OpenAI cautioned that a doubled allowance does not translate into twice as many completed tasks, because consumption depends on the model, the type of task and the settings a user picks. The company pointed to efficiency gains, including its recent 6.1 models Terra and Sol, which it says match or beat their predecessors while using fewer resources.
The Decoder connected the move to the competition between OpenAI and Anthropic for business customers as Anthropic prepares for its initial public offering.

The reversal is the second change to Pro 200 in a month, and it shows how sensitive heavy users have become to usage caps on agent and coding tools. By raising allowances instead of cutting prices, OpenAI keeps its plan structure intact while answering the complaints, but it leaves subscribers on the $20 Plus plan without any added capacity.
The next thing to watch is whether OpenAI publishes concrete per plan numbers for Work and Codex usage, including the Business Premium seat, and whether the Plus plan receives a similar increase.
